description:
Portmaster is a free and open-source application that puts you back in charge over all your computers network connections.

Portmaster is a free and open-source application firewall that does the heavy lifting for you. Restore privacy and take back control over all your computer's network activity.

Discover everything that is happening on your computer. Expose every connection your applications make and detect evil ones. Finally get the power to act accordingly.

Protect your whole computer, not just your browser. Block all advertisements and trackers for every application. Easily add your own rules and block individual domains.

Make your own rules. Completely cut off applications from the Internet. Or block all p2p connections except for certain apps. Or never connect to specific countries. Portmaster has you covered.
What's Changed
- fix: (Linux) High memory usage and verdict timeouts during bursts of new connections by @stenya in #2279 and #2293
- fix: (Linux) Crash in iptables maintenance when another tool flushed the chains by @stenya in c6810cb
- fix: (Linux) UDP split tunnel proxy bound to the wrong loopback address by @JacksonBarker in #2266
- fix: (Linux) UI crash on Wayland with the NVIDIA driver ("Error 71 (Protocol error)") by @stenya in #1898
- fix: (Windows) Random UI crashes (0xc000001d / 0xc0000374) by @stenya in #2281
- (Windows) Kernel driver 2.1.2 by @stenya in #2285 and #2284:
  - fix: Service could stay in "Stopping" until reboot (together with a core fix)
  - fix: System crash (BugCheck 0x50) when a second client closed its driver handle
  - fix: A new connection on a recently closed port could inherit the previous verdict
  - improvement: Driver panic now triggers a dedicated bug check instead of DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION
- fix: Intermittent DNS failures on reserved local ports by @stenya and @dannyagostinelli in #2272
- fix: DNS resolution could break until restart after all DNS servers were marked as failing by @stenya in #2294 b543aba
- fix: Filter list base updates did not purge obsolete entries or rebuild bloom filters by @stenya in #2300
- fix: (Windows) Geo rules failed with "data not available" after an intel update by @stenya in #2265
- fix: Failed profile lookup left connections without a verdict and blocked process exit by @stenya in #2275
- fix: Connections blocked when ASN/country data was missing despite allow rules by @stenya in #2138
- fix: Path traversal via artifact filenames in the update index by @stenya in a9d919f
- fix: Removed an unauthenticated local API endpoint that could install an older signed release by @stenya in #2292
- fix: (UI) "Edit App Profile" kept changes after "Cancel" by @stenya in #2165
- fix: (UI) Rule selection counter out of sync; "Remove Rules" could delete the wrong rules by @stenya in #2164
- fix: (UI) Tray icon ignored the OS theme when the icon theme was "System" by @stenya in #2222
- fix: (UI) App page did not reliably close after the profile ID changed by @stenya in 74b16e2
- fix: (UI) "Open Data Directory" did nothing; it now opens the system file manager by @stenya in #1834
- improvement: Bloom filter capacities raised to match current filter list sizes by @stenya in 760cd47
- improvement: Filter list imports are about twice as fast on the database side by @stenya in b56aba0
- improvement: (Linux) LOGLEVEL from /etc/default/portmaster is now applied by @stenya in aea3aa4

New Contributors
- @JacksonBarker made their first contribution in #2266

Special Thanks
- @dannyagostinelli for analysing the DNS bind failures and proposing the fix in #2267, which #2272 builds on
